title: Ad creative generator
description:
Long-term position for the right person!



About Us

Kickin Bikes and RFN (Racing Fears Nothing) are electric dirt bike brands based in the US. RFN runs the Warrior Series line. We move fast, test a lot of creative, and rely heavily on AI tools for marketing production.



The Role

We need someone who can independently turn existing footage and brand direction into scroll-stopping video ad creatives for Meta, YouTube, and native ad platforms — using AI generation tools. You’ll take a source video, a hook, and a persona/angle, and produce polished, ready-to-run ad variations without needing your hand held through the process.

This is NOT an entry-level or “I’ll learn as I go” role. We’re looking for someone who already has real reps in AI video generation and ad creative production, and who has good creative taste. If you need to be taught the fundamentals or your output needs heavy revision, this isn’t the right fit — and that’s okay, we just need someone else.

What You’ll Do

 • Take existing edited videos and generate new AI-powered ad variations (different hooks, personas, angles, styles)

 • Use Higgsfield AI and ChatGPT to produce and iterate on video/image creative for Meta, YouTube, and native ad campaigns

 • Turn brief creative direction (delivered 1–2x/week) into a batch of finished, ready-to-test assets

 • Maintain brand consistency across RFN and Kickin Bikes while adapting tone/style per platform

 • Flag what’s working and suggest new creative angles proactively — we want a creative partner, not just an order-taker

 • Organize and deliver finished files in an easy-to-review format (Drive folder, naming conventions, etc.)

What We Need From You

 • 2+ years of hands-on experience with AI ad creative and/or AI video generation tools (Higgsfield, Runway, Kling, Veo, or similar)

 • A portfolio or work samples of AI-generated ad creatives you’ve produced — this is required, not optional

 • Strong creative instincts — you know what makes an ad hook work and what looks cheap or off-brand

 • Ability to work independently from light direction; we check in 1–2x/week, not daily

 • Comfortable with ChatGPT for prompt writing and creative ideation

 • Reliable, deadline-driven, communicates proactively when something’s blocked

 • Good English communication for async updates (Slack/email)

Tools Provided

We cover your Higgsfield AI and ChatGPT subscriptions. You just need a reliable computer and internet connection.

Schedule & Pay

 • ~4 hours/day, flexible within reason, some overlap with US hours preferred for check-ins

 • Pay: DOE — we pay above typical rates for real experience, since we’d rather pay more for someone who doesn’t need training than pay less and manage someone closely

 • Long-term, ongoing work if it’s a good fit on both sides

To Apply

Send:

 1. Your resume/work history. 

 2. A portfolio or 3–5 sample AI-generated ad creatives (links or files) — applications without samples won’t be considered. 

 3. A one-paragraph note on your experience with Higgsfield AI (or whichever AI video tool you’ve used most) and what platforms you’ve made ad creative for. 

 4. Start your application with the word “HOOKS” so we know you read the full post. 

We’re looking to move quickly for the right candidate.

title: Team Media Buyer (Facebook/Meta, YouTube/Google Ads)
description:
We are Singapore’s fastest growing performance real estate business seeking



Media Buyer (Direct Response | Performance-Focused)

Part-Time | Remote



About Singapore Real Estate Insider



We are a Singapore-based property agent agency working with 1st time homeowner, HDB owners, Private property owners, Landed owners and investors across Singapore. We specialise in property related services — consulting, advisory, selling, buying, renting, investment, portfolio management and legacy planning — where real money is spent daily and performance matters.



We’re also part of a broader group that operates:

Millionaire Agent (our education & mentoring brand for fellow agents)

Family Legacy Launch (our education & mentoring brand for home owners)



All brands are owned and operated by the same team. This role sits fully within the Singapore Real Estate Insider performance team.





Why This Role Is Different



This is not a branding or “boost post” role.



You’ll be working on:

- Real conversion campaigns

- Meaningful daily ad spend

- Funnels where decisions have real impact



You’ll follow proven SOPs — and you’ll also be trusted to make judgment calls when performance requires it.



If you want to grow fast by working close to real data, real money, and real decisions, this role will stretch you in the right way.





What You’ll Do



- Run and optimise conversion-focused paid ad campaigns (Meta primarily & YouTube next)

- Monitor campaign performance and flag issues early

- Own campaign health, not just execution

- Follow SOPs by default and make informed adjustments when needed

- Writing ad copy or designing creatives

- Redesigning funnels, offers, or pricing

- Handling client communication or account management

- Juggling multiple stakeholders or unclear priorities



Your focus is campaign performance and health, with clear boundaries and structure. And any platform design and inputs to optimize the entire ad and reporting process.





Who This Role Is For

This role is a good fit if you:

- Have hands-on experience running conversion ads (leads or sales)

- Are comfortable in performance-driven environments

- Stay calm, analytical, and accountable when things move fast

- Respect structure but don’t freeze when conditions change

- Communicate clearly and take ownership seriously



Who This Role Is NOT For

- “Set-and-forget” ad managers

- Freelancers juggling multiple clients

- People looking for a low-pressure, purely 9–5 role

- Anyone uncomfortable with responsibility tied to real spend





Compensation & Growth



At Singapore Real Estate Insider, compensation is more than a monthly paycheck.



You’ll be operating in an ecosystem where:

- 6-figures are spent on paid ads monthly

- Multiple six figures are invested yearly into business, operations, education, health, and performance

- Decisions are made using real data, real risk, and real outcomes



What This Means for You

- Exposure to high-spend, direct-response campaigns

- Learn world-class media buying and direct response practices

- Grow beyond ads — into business thinking, systems, and personal performance

- Performance bonuses for strong execution and decision-making

- Opportunities to join yearly team retreats and overseas events held a few times a year



If you’re looking for comfort, this isn’t it.



If you’re looking to level up fast and grow properly, you’ll thrive here.



The questions are designed to understand how you think, not just what tools you’ve used.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.



Final Note

We’re not looking for button-pushers.

We’re looking for media buyers who:

Respect structure

Protect campaign performance

Take ownership seriously

If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

title: Medical Biller
description:
Part-Time Medical Biller (Tebra) — Mental Health Practice



Type: Part-time, remote (Philippines-based)

Pay: $7.50–$8.00/hour to start, based on experience (in line with current OnlineJobs.ph rates for this role), reviewed after the first 60 days

Hours: Start at roughly 8–10 hours/week for the first month (to clear a backlog audit), then settling into approximately 5 hours/week ongoing. Flexible schedule, but needs some overlap availability for occasional questions during US business hours (Pacific Time preferred).



About Us



ReNurture is a telehealth mental health practice based in California, providing psychiatric medication management and therapy services. We opened in December 2025 and use Tebra (formerly Kareo) for scheduling, encounters, and billing. We're a small, growing practice and need a dedicated part-time biller to keep our insurance billing clean, current, and fully collected — this isn't a full-time role, just consistent, reliable hours each week.



The Role



We need someone who can first audit everything we've billed (and not billed) since we opened, fix what's broken, and then maintain it going forward with a standing weekly billing cadence. You'll work directly in Tebra and report findings/progress to the practice owner weekly.



Phase 1 — One-Time Backlog Audit (first 2–4 weeks)



Review the full A/R Aging Detail report since December 2025 and identify every open claim by payer, age, and status.

Run the Missed Charges report across our full history to find any completed appointment that never generated a charge.

Pull the full Claim Record Log, filtered to No Response, Rejected, and Denied statuses, for the entire practice history — not just the current snapshot.

For every aged or silent claim, check its Clearinghouse Tracking # and transaction history to determine if it was actually received/accepted by the payer, versus lost or rejected.

Flag anything at risk of missing a payer's timely filing deadline and prioritize those first.

Verify our payer enrollment/credentialing dates lined up correctly with when we started billing each payer (Aetna, Cigna, Medicare, UHC).

Deliver a written summary: what's outstanding, what's genuinely at risk, what's been fixed, and what still needs a decision from us (e.g., write-offs, appeals).





Phase 2 — Ongoing Weekly Billing (standing responsibility)



Submit all new claims ready for electronic submission on a weekly schedule.

Post payments, EOBs, and ERAs as they come in.

Work the No Response / Rejected / Denied claims queue every week — don't let anything sit past a payer's normal response window without a follow-up action.

Run the Missed Charges report weekly to catch any unbilled visit within days, not months.

Follow up directly with payers (portal or phone) on anything stuck or unusually delayed.

Send a short weekly summary to the practice owner: what was billed, what was collected, what's still open, and anything that needs attention.





What You Need to Bring



Direct hands-on experience with Tebra (or Kareo) — this is close to a requirement, not a nice-to-have. You should already be comfortable with Find Claim/Track Claim Status, Clearinghouse Reports, the Rebill workflow, and running Analytics reports.

Solid U.S. medical billing experience; behavioral/mental health billing experience is a strong plus (familiarity with codes like 99214/99215, 90833/90836/90838, 96127, and telehealth modifier 95).

Working knowledge of major U.S. payers: Aetna, Cigna, Medicare, and UnitedHealthcare — how each one behaves, typical turnaround times, and how to work a denial or appeal with them.

Understanding of timely filing rules and how to prioritize aged claims before they become unrecoverable.

Sharp attention to detail — this role exists specifically because things fell through the cracks before, so we need someone who won't let that happen again.

Comfortable working independently and proactively flagging problems rather than waiting to be asked.

Good written English for weekly reporting and occasional async questions.

Reliable internet and your own equipment.





How to Apply



To confirm you've read this closely, start your application with the word "Claims" as the first word of your message, and briefly describe one billing issue you've caught and fixed for a past client that the client hadn't noticed on their own. Include your experience with Tebra/Kareo specifically, your available weekly hours, and your expected rate.

title: Appointment Setter
description:
TO APPLY, READ THE JOB BRIEF IN FULL, THEN FILL OUT THE QUICK

TYPEFORM APPLICATION HERE: https://form.typeform.com/to/RkOnVtOA



IF YOU DO NOT DO THIS, YOU WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED.





Appointment Setter / Sales Pipeline Owner — DTC SEO Agency

Type: Full-time, remote. Must work US Central business hours (we're based in Austin, TX). Non-negotiable.



Reports to: Thomas (fixed weekly 15-min scorecard review). Day-to-day, you own your own numbers in the tracker; the tracker is the accountability mechanism.



Comp: Flat base at your quoted monthly rate.



Commitment: Long-term. This is not a 3-month gig; we want someone who grows with the company.

Why this role exists: Right now inbound leads go un-worked, booked calls no-show, reschedules get dropped, and two-plus years of previous leads sit untouched across old CRMs. This role owns everything between "a lead exists" and "Thomas is on the call," then fills downtime with partner outreach. You own this pipeline; you don't wait to be told.



1. Speed-to-lead (daily, time-critical)



Text and call every new inbound within 5 minutes during working hours.

Pre-qualify against the qualified-call standard (below). Get them excited to talk to Thomas as an SEO expert.

Book qualified leads straight onto Thomas's calendar.



2. Calendar & booking authority



Own Thomas's sales calendar. Load his availability live on calls and book the time directly.

Authority to move and reschedule bookings to keep the slate full and pull calls earlier (closer booking = higher show rate).



3. Show-rate protection



Confirm every booked call twice (24h and 1h prior) by text/call.

Standard: every confirmable call gets confirmed, no exceptions.

Where a call is booked far out, work to pull it earlier.



4. Reschedule recovery (daily, zero-drop)



Any lead who asks to reschedule gets called/texted the same day to lock a new time. No reschedule sits unanswered.



5. Reactivation (front-loaded first weeks, then ongoing)



Work previous leads across all old CRMs: GHL funnel, dormant iClosed leads, ClickUp audited-but-unclosed clients.

Re-engage and book onto Thomas's calendar. Audit angle: "we ran your audit a while back, things have likely changed, worth a fresh look with Thomas?"

This is gold sitting untouched; treat it as a priority, not a someday task.



6. Pre-call prep



Before each discovery call, research the lead: website, LinkedIn, revenue signals, current SEO state.

Hand Thomas a one-page brief so he walks in fully prepped.



7. Funnel optimization (ownership, not just execution)



Own the SendBlue text and Gmail
 sequences for inbound and booked leads.

Plug the unbooked-lead gap (form-fillers who don't book currently get nothing). Build a 3-touch sequence (text,
, text over ~5 days).

Test variants of the opener text to lift reply rate; bring 2-3 versions with reasoning, not just "send more."

Sharpen the pre-call
 series to build show-up urgency and lightly re-qualify.

Flag where an automated message should become a manual personal touch (or vice versa).

Judge all changes on the numbers: opener reply rate, show rate, book rate.



8. Onboarding handoff (on close)



When Thomas closes a client: grab the Fathom link, set up the ClickUp folder, alert the team to start.



9. Partner outreach (downtime / overflow capacity)



Find agencies, consultants, and heads of growth serving $5M+ DTC ecommerce brands.

Reach out via
 and LinkedIn; book them onto Thomas's calendar.

Pitch and book Thomas as a guest on the partner's podcast where relevant (gives the partner value, builds the relationship).

Send Thomas's weekly YouTube video to the partner DB as a recurring top-of-mind touch; log it.



10. Tracker ownership (ongoing)



Build and maintain the single source of truth for every lead and partner: source, stage, last contact, next action, owner.

Current and accurate at all times. Nothing lives in anyone's head.



11. Calling stack setup (week 1 task)



Set up and test the web-app dialer with Krisp accent converter. Confirm live-call quality and latency. If Krisp doesn't cut it, find and test an alternative. This is yours to own.





Qualified call standard (a lead only reaches Thomas's calendar if ALL are true):



Ecommerce brand (hard requirement)

$5M+ annual revenue (ICP), or $1M+ with clear budget

Product-market fit: real product, real demand

Scaling profitably with paid ads



Sub-$1M or unqualified leads get routed to partners or disqualified. Booking unqualified leads to pad the count is the one way to fail this role while looking busy.



KPIs (tracked weekly, these define whether the job is being done):



Speed-to-lead: 90%+ of inbound contacted within 5 min (working hours)

5 qualified calls booked per week from reactivation

Show rate: 85-90% of booked calls held; every confirmable call confirmed twice

Reschedules recovered same-day: 100%

Partner conversations booked for Thomas: monthly target (feeds the ~20 partnerships/mo goal)

Tracker current at every weekly review



These aren't bonus targets, they're the standard. Clearing them keeps the seat; missing them consistently triggers the 30-day kill criteria.

Tools: iClosed (booking), SendBlue (texts), web-app dialer + Krisp (calls), GHL, ClickUp, Gmail, LinkedIn, Fathom.

Must-haves: US Central hours (non-negotiable). Fluent, natural spoken English. Phone-confident and able to pre-qualify. Self-directed; owns a tracker without reminders. Appointment-setting or phone sales experience. Hungry, long-term, goes above the bare minimum.

title: Google Ads Manager, Professional Services Lead Generation (US Tax Advisory Firm)
description:
Job Title: Google Ads Manager, Professional Services Lead Generation (US Tax Advisory Firm)



Type: Part-time contractor, ongoing monthly retainer

Hours: 10-15 professional hours per month

Schedule: Flexible. Must be available for a 30-minute check-in call every two weeks during US Eastern business hours 11 am-2 pm ET / 11 pm-2 am PHT).

Compensation: . Negotiable for candidates who can demonstrate 5+ years of documented professional services PPC management with verifiable results.



---



The Firm



Simonsgroup Tax Advisory is a strategic tax planning firm in Washington, DC. Not tax preparation. Not seasonal filing. Our clients are business owners ($300K-$5M revenue), high-income tech professionals, and real estate investors. Engagement values range from $1,800 to $10,000+.



The Google Ads account runs Search campaigns in the DC, Maryland, and Northern Virginia metro area. Monthly ad spend: approximately $2,000. The only conversion that matters: intake form submissions that result in booked advisory consultations.



---



Why This Role Exists



The account has been through three vendor relationships in eight months. Each produced the same pattern: generic reporting without actual data, keyword strategies that attracted tax preparation shoppers instead of advisory clients, and tracking configurations that inflated conversion counts while real lead quality degraded.



Two independent audits have been completed. A separate Phase 1 engagement will fix the structural and tracking issues those audits identified (GA4 misconfiguration, conversion tag duplication, broken Enhanced Conversions, campaign restructuring, landing page alignment). Phase 1 must be complete before this engagement begins.



This role picks up after the foundation is repaired. Your job: keep the data clean, keep the budget protected from waste, and steadily improve cost per qualified lead.



---



Weekly: Search Term and Negative Keyword Management (4-5 hours/month)



The most important recurring task. Corporate tax keywords cost $10-$25 per click. Without weekly review, Google's algorithms will match your ads to consumer tax prep queries, IRS self-service searches, competitor name lookups, and job seekers within days. This has been documented and measured in this account.



Every week:



- Pull the search terms report for the prior 7 days

- Review every query that generated a click

- Add negative keywords for competitor names, consumer queries ("free tax services," "file my taxes"), IRS self-service queries ("irs payment plan," "form 9465"), job seeker queries ("bookkeeping jobs remote"), and out-of-market locations

- All negatives as phrase match. Not exact match. Exact match negatives let variants through. This has been a recurring vendor failure on this account.

- Maintain a running log: date, keyword, match type, rationale

- Flag any emerging search pattern that suggests a keyword or ad group adjustment



Weekly means weekly. A competitor name that collects 3 clicks before it is blocked costs $30-$75.



---



Bi-weekly: Performance Monitoring and Bid Management (2-3 hours/month)



- Flag any keyword with $75+ spend and zero conversions over a rolling 30-day window

- Monitor geographic performance. DC and Maryland convert. Virginia locations have historically shown near-zero activity. Diagnose and recommend if that pattern continues.

- Monitor device performance. Mobile has consistently outperformed desktop on conversion rate in this account.

- Verify ad scheduling restricts spend to business hours. No serving between 10pm and 6am.

- Review auction insights monthly. Track competitive position against 
, H&R Block, and Intuit.



---



Bi-weekly: Reporting (2-3 hours/month)



Written report every two weeks. Data, not descriptions. Every report includes:



- Spend by campaign and ad group

- Impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, conversions, cost per conversion by ad group

- Search impression share: total, lost to budget, lost to rank

- Top-of-page rate and absolute top-of-page rate

- Quality scores for top 10 keywords by spend (including Landing Page Experience, Ad Relevance, Expected CTR sub-scores)

- Auction insights: top 5 competitors by impression share

- Top 15 search terms by spend with clicks, cost, conversions

- Negative keywords added during the period (from the running log)

- Location performance by targeted area

- Device performance breakdown

- Conversion action health: verify tag is firing, confirm primary/secondary configuration, reconcile Google Ads conversions against Tally form submission count

- Actions taken since last report (specific changes, not descriptions of process)

- Recommendations for next period with rationale



Reports that describe what a metric means without providing the actual number will not be accepted. Three consecutive vendors delivered reports with section headers and metric definitions but no data. That is the standard this role replaces.



---



Monthly: Ad Copy Testing (1-2 hours/month)



- Maintain at least 3 responsive search ad variations per ad group

- Test headlines reflecting advisory positioning: S-Corp strategy, entity structuring, high-income tax planning, real estate investor tax, IRS resolution

- Pause underperformers based on CTR and conversion rate. Not ad strength scores.

- Ensure ad copy aligns with landing page content



---



Ongoing: Conversion Tracking Integrity



Phase 1 fixes the tracking. This role keeps it clean.



- Test the intake form conversion tag quarterly (submit a test form, confirm it registers in Google Ads)

- Monitor for double-counting anomalies (any keyword with a conversion rate above 100% gets investigated immediately)

- Verify conversion values remain correctly assigned ($200-$500 per lead type)

- Reconcile Google Ads click count against GA4 paid sessions monthly

- Reconcile reported conversions against Tally submission count bi-weekly



The account has a documented history of tracking failures that corrupted Smart Bidding. Ongoing verification is not optional.



---



Required Experience



Minimum 5 years managing Google Ads Search campaigns for professional services firms: law firms, accounting firms, financial advisory, tax advisory, consulting, or medical practices. You must have managed at least 3 accounts in this category over that period.



General experience with e-commerce, local trades (plumbing, HVAC, landscaping), or app install campaigns does not substitute. The keyword economics, conversion paths, and lead quality standards for a $5,000 advisory engagement are fundamentally different from a $200 service call.



Additional requirements:



- Demonstrated experience with form-based or consultation-based conversion tracking, not e-commerce transactions

- Proficient with impression share analysis, quality score diagnostics, auction insights, and search term management at the query level

- Understands how conversion action configuration (primary vs. secondary, count setting, attribution window, value assignment) affects Smart Bidding behavior

- Can diagnose geographic targeting issues (e.g., algorithm deprioritizing specific locations due to budget constraints)

- Clear, data-driven written reporting in English

- Works in the client's own Google Ads account via MCC access



Preferred:



- Experience managing campaigns in the US professional services market

- Familiarity with Tally, Calendly, or similar form/scheduling-based conversion tracking

- Experience with Maximize Conversions and Target CPA bidding transitions

- Google Ads Search certification



---



Account Access



The Google Ads account is owned by Simonsgroup. You receive manager-level access via MCC. Account ownership does not transfer. All campaigns, keywords, ads, conversion tracking, and work product remain in the Simonsgroup account. If the engagement ends, the account continues with no disruption.



---



Timezone



The firm operates on US Eastern time. Bi-weekly check-in calls: 8am-12pm ET (8pm-12am PHT). Async communication via
 for everything else. Responsiveness within 24 hours on business days is expected.



---



How to Apply



Answer all four questions. Applications that skip any question or send a generic cover letter will not be reviewed.



1. Name 2-3 professional services firms (law, accounting, financial advisory, medical) where you managed Google Ads on a monthly retainer for at least 6 months. For each: monthly ad spend, qualified leads per month, cost per qualified lead, and the single most impactful change you made. Anonymize client names if needed.



2. You pull this week's search terms report and see 8 of the top 20 queries by spend are people searching for specific CPA names ("john smith cpa," "abc tax services"). They generated $110 in clicks and zero conversions. What do you do, what match type for the negatives, and why that match type?



3. Google Ads shows 4 conversions this period. The intake form platform shows 7 submissions. What are the possible explanations and what would you check first?



4. Your monthly rate for this scope and hours.



Applications that answer all four questions with specifics will be prioritized. The next step is a short paid test task (compensated at your rate) before any ongoing engagement begins.

After 17+ years in breaking—including pioneering high-volume, vulnerable storytelling with the #NicosYear 365-day project in

My focus is authentic content about overcoming adversity (early family losses that forced me to grow up fast), resilience, fatherhood, real business challenges, and turning setbacks into strengths. The goal is to build genuine trust and a supportive community through organic, value-driven content that resonates with people on similar journeys—no quick sales or courses, just evergreen trust and leads that strengthen my family businesses over time.

. Tools include Adobe Premiere/Express, Opus Pro for efficient clipping, and smart AI prompting to maximize output.

title: Exceptionally Detail Oriented Video Editor
description:
Hello!



I’m Jesse, a real estate company, based in the Twin Cities of Minnesota in the USA, but I come from a creative background; musician, photographer and videographer. I've taken that experience and grown my business over the past 6+ years, and I have been lucky enough to find a few incredible remote employees from the Philippines primarily as video editors. My relationship to them has been so valuable to me and still is, but now I'm hoping to find some more help, specifically with some very detail oriented video editing for a new video series I'm adding to our channel.



The primary thing I'm looking for in an editor is talent and a creative eye and an ability to work with large video sessions, often editing 20-40 minute videos that includes talking head footage, b-roll as well as screen recordings and map graphics that YOU will be responsible for tracking down and/or creating. Over the years, I find video editors often want to work with multiple clients, and that's okay with me as long as my videos are a priority to you, and you can get them done in a timely manner - typically one long form videos per week or two, plus a couple short form videos derived from the main video. If a full time position would work better for you, please let me know and we can discuss what that can look like.  As a team we have a LOT of videos to edit.



I started a business because I was tired of having bosses who didn't care about my goals and ambitions. For that reason, it is very important to me to provide an employee with the ability to grow and increase their income and improve their position in life through hard work and creative problem solving. I am hoping to find somebody driven and hard-working who has a keen, creative eye and will be invested in the success of our business, and I will reward that effort and dedication. I have filmed and posted over a thousand videos in the past 6 years, and I've edited many many more before that, so I'm very familiar with the workload and process, I just need a great partner to help me get it done.



If this sounds like something you would be interested in, and I sound like the kind of person you'd want to work with, send a portfolio link and I ask that the subject of the message you send say “Hi Jesse, I'm your detail-oriented editor” followed by the name of the video editing software you use. If you don't follow that instruction, you won't be considered. 



If we have an interview, I will ask you to perform a test edit from the raw video files I have - typically working in 4K Sony log footage. If you aren't familiar with color grading, and editing with music, dialogue, b-roll and large file sizes, I'm not sure we'll be the right fit as there's a learning curve to some of these basics.



One last thing - include as much variety as possible in your portfolio.  It's entirely possible you aren't the right fit for this project, but perfect for a different video series.



Thanks so much,



Jesse

title: Content Strategist/Social Media Manager
description:
This is not an entry-level role. We need someone who has done this before, can prove it, and has a clear system for how they work.



About the brand

Keenya Kelly is a video marketing and monetization strategist with a large established audience across TikTok, Instagram, and
. We teach entrepreneurs how to grow through short vertical video and turn their content into consistent income. We have an active offer ecosystem including a membership, a flagship course, and low-ticket funnels. We are a systems-driven team that operates with clear processes, deadlines, and communication standards.



What we are looking for:



You have a proven framework or methodology for creating content that grows accounts AND drives revenue. Not just views. Not just followers. Actual conversions and sales.



You can show us accounts you have worked on, what the numbers looked like before you got involved, and what happened after.



You think in systems. You do not wing it. You have a repeatable process for researching a brand, building a content strategy, and delivering direction that a team can execute consistently.



You understand the difference between content that builds an audience and content that converts that audience into buyers — and you know how to build both into a strategy at the same time.



You can execute what you strategize. You are not just handing off a plan and walking away — you are scripting, captioning, and directing the actual content alongside your strategy.



What this role involves



Deep dive into the Keenya Kelly brand — audience, offers, voice, content pillars, and competitors — and develop a content strategy tailored to where we are going, not just where we have been.



Deliver weekly content for Instagram,
, and TikTok — including hooks, format direction, scripts, captions, and CTAs that connect to our active offers.



Deliver a Trial Reels concept per day for Instagram.



Build and hand over a content system our team can run — including a competitor database, hook library, and content direction framework.



Join bi-weekly strategy calls to review performance and align on the next content cycle.



Adapt content direction quickly during active launch periods — we run live challenges, webinars, and course launch campaigns that require content to shift with the offer.



Manage day-to-day execution on the accounts you are directing — scheduling, captioning, and staying on top of what is live.



You are the right person if



You have a documented system or framework for content strategy — not just experience, an actual repeatable process.



You can show us at least two accounts you have grown that also became more profitable — with before and after numbers.



You understand short vertical video deeply — TikTok, Instagram Reels, and
 — and you know how to build strategy differently for each platform.



You are highly organized and can deliver on deadlines without being chased.



You are comfortable working alongside a brand owner who is also a strategist — you do not need to own the entire process to do your best work.



You communicate proactively



You can move fast between strategy and execution without needing a separate person to hand things off to.



This is not the right role if



You need to control the entire process in order to stand behind your strategy.



You are still building your process and learning as you go.



You cannot provide proof of accounts you have grown and monetized.



You struggle with structure, deadlines, or communicating your own process clearly.



You only want to strategize and do not want to touch execution.



How to apply

Your application must include:



A brief description of your content strategy framework or system



how you approach a new brand from day one



Two or more examples of accounts you have grown and helped monetize include the platform, the follower growth, and the revenue or conversion results



Applications that do not include proof of results will not be reviewed.

About the Role



We are hiring a full-time Customer Support Representative to own the customer experience across Amazon, Walmart, and Shopify.



This is an ownership role, not a ticket-closing role. You will be the first point of contact for customers, resolve every case end to end, and help protect our Amazon and Walmart account health. Your written communication represents our brand with every message.



This is a long-term, single-employer position. We are looking for someone who wants to grow with one company, not a freelancer balancing multiple clients.



Responsibilities



Respond to customer inquiries across
, Amazon and Walmart marketplace messaging, and our Shopify store within defined response-time targets

Own each case from first contact to resolution, including follow-up on shipping, tracking, lost-package, and delivery-exception issues with carriers

Manage returns, replacements, refunds, and address or fulfillment errors, coordinating with our warehouse and operations team

Monitor and respond to reviews and seller feedback (Amazon, Walmart, Trustpilot), and pursue removal of policy-violating or resolved negative reviews

Flag listing accuracy, content, and inventory discrepancies to the catalog and operations teams with clear documentation

Maintain accurate records and follow established SOPs, suggesting improvements where gaps exist

Escalate complex or at-risk accounts (including B2B and wholesale buyers) promptly

Complete a short daily check-in on weekends (20 to 30 minutes per day) to keep marketplace response times compliant



Requirements



2+ years in customer support, ideally in e-commerce or retail

Hands-on experience with at least one major marketplace (Amazon Seller Central strongly preferred; Walmart and Shopify a plus)

Excellent written English and a professional, customer-first tone

Strong organization and follow-through, working independently in a remote setting

Comfortable with help-desk or ticketing tools and basic spreadsheets

Reliable internet connection and a quiet home working setup

Full commitment: no other clients or roles



Nice to Have



Experience with returns and carrier claims (USPS, UPS, FedEx)

Familiarity with review-management and feedback tools

Experience supporting B2B or wholesale accounts



What We Offer



Competitive monthly salary plus performance bonus

100% remote, long-term stable role with a growing US brand

Paid time off

Direct ownership of your function, with a small team that moves fast



How to Apply



 your resume to 
 with the subject line: Customer Support Representative — [Your Name]



In the body of your
, answer these three questions:



Briefly describe your experience handling customer messages on Amazon or Walmart (or another marketplace).

Tell us about a difficult customer issue you resolved end to end. What was the situation and what did you do?

Why does this role interest you, and are you comfortable with a short daily check-in on weekends?



Applications without answers to all three questions will not be reviewed.



We are moving quickly. Strong candidates will hear back fast.

title: Shopify Ecom Inventory Management/Manager
description:
Hi,



We are running a brand that is doing 50,000+ units a month with over 20 skus with the inventory both in China and USA.



Right now I am spending countless hours calculating when we need to re-order more inventory, if our USA 3pl is running low on inventory and when we need to send more to that location, etc. 



It takes 2-3 weeks for our product to be created in the factory whenever we place a new order. If we want to send the product to our USA 3PL that takes another 30 days to arrive by boat as well. 



About 60% of our orders are USA and being shipped from USA warehouse, the rest are international and being shipped from our China warehouse.



We are looking to hire an inventory manager that can manage all of this.



We need you to

Have clean data, clear reorder points, and actually knowing your sales velocity and lead times

Make sure USA inventory always has 60+ days of stock and China inventory always has 60+ days of stock in all 20+ flavors. 



Not sure if you would like to use some app to track all of this or how the best way to go about it is. I've seen some people using inventory mate or shipgenius, whatever works best we are down to use or what you've used in past for other brands. 



Please only apply if you have experience doing this, we are already a big brand and need experienced person to properly manage all of our inventory.

title: Shopify Specialist -- Store Audit, SEO & B2B
description:
Shopify Specialist -- Store Audit, SEO & B2B

One-off project (fixed price) - with ongoing maintenance opportunity - Remote

Help a family-run Queensland farm business get its Shopify store found, converting, and set up for wholesale



Type One-off project to start (fixed price), with the opportunity for ongoing maintenance if it's a good fit

Platform Shopify

Focus Getting found (SEO), improving the store (design, layout, product pages, conversion), and setting up B2B wholesale ordering

First step An audit with clear recommendations and a plan -- we'll then d
 together what to action

Payment Please quote a fixed price for the audit + recommendations stage

Start As soon as we find the right person



About us

We are a family-run agribusiness in rural Queensland, Australia, selling premium Wagyu and grass-fed beef and a range of value-added products (and natural skincare) direct to customers. We sell online through our Shopify store as well as at markets and direct to venues.

What we want to achieve

Our Shopify store is not working as hard as it should, and we want your expert help on three fronts:

• Get found (SEO): We want to show up better in Google searches so more of the right people discover us.

• Improve the store: People who visit are not converting into buyers the way we would like. We want the store looking professional, easy to navigate, and set up to turn visitors into customers.

• Set up B2B & beast orders: We sell to venues (restaurants, pubs, clubs) but have no wholesale/B2B ordering on the site, and we want proper whole, half and quarter beast order forms for our direct customers. We would like these built into the store.

The project -- how we would like to work

We would like to start with an audit, clear recommendations, and a plan -- rather than jumping straight into changes. The first piece of paid work is:

1. Review our Shopify store -- its search visibility (SEO), the store itself (design, layout, product pages, conversion), and how best to add B2B wholesale ordering and whole/half/quarter beast order forms.

2. Give us a clear, plain-English report of what is working, what is not, and what you would recommend -- prioritised, biggest impact first.

3. Include a plan and quote for actioning the fixes and building the B2B / beast-order functionality, so we can d
 together what to go ahead with.

Note on B2B: we understand Shopify handles wholesale ordering in different ways depending on plan and apps -- part of what we would value from your audit is your recommendation on the best, most cost-effective way to do this for our store.

Once we have seen the audit and plan, we will d
 what to action -- and there is a strong opportunity for the right person to carry out the work and take on ongoing maintenance of the store.

What we are looking for

• Proven Shopify experience -- you know the platform inside out (themes, product pages, collections, store setup, apps).

• Experience setting up B2B / wholesale ordering and custom order forms on Shopify.

• Real SEO experience -- improving how a store ranks and gets found in Google (on-page SEO, product/collection optimisation, site structure, speed).

• A good eye for design and user experience -- making a store look professional, trustworthy, and easy to buy from.

• An understanding of conversion -- what actually turns visitors into buyers, not just what looks nice.

• Clear written English and the ability to explain things simply (we are not technical -- we need plain language).

Please be honest about where your strengths lie. Some people are stronger on SEO, others on store design and build -- if you are excellent at one and solid at the others, that is fine, just tell us.

How to apply

Applications that answer the questions below will be prioritised. Please send:

4. A short note on your Shopify, SEO and B2B experience, and where your main strength lies.

5. Links to 2-3 Shopify stores you have worked on -- ideally ones you improved the visibility or conversion of, or set up wholesale/B2B for, with a note on what you did.

6. Your fixed price to complete the audit + recommendations + plan stage described above, and roughly how long it would take.

And -- most importantly -- please take a quick look at our actual store and answer:

• Having looked at our Shopify store, what are the top 3-4 things you would prioritise to help us get found and convert more visitors into buyers? (Just your key observations -- the full detail is what the paid audit is for.)

This does not need to be a full audit -- we just want to see that you have actually looked at our store and can spot what matters. We are genuinely open to your expertise, so if you see something we have not thought of, we would love to hear it.
salary: 500$ one off payment when site is fixed

title: Personal / Executive Assistant — Long-Term, Full-Time Role
description:
PERSONAL / EXECUTIVE ASSISTANT — LONG-TERM, FULL-TIME ROLE



Remote | $8/hr, bi-weekly pay | 9am–5pm US Pacific



WHO I AM



I'm an entrepreneur based in Southern California. I run a digital marketing agency serving home-service businesses, and I'm a coach inside a paid coaching program for marketing agency owners. Between the two, I manage roughly 80 client and member relationships.



You can check me 
 on instagram, 



THE ROLE



You will be MY assistant. Not the agency's assistant, not the coaching program's assistant — mine. Your job is to protect my time, carry my communication load, and make my life simpler. The work happens to live mostly inside client success and member communication, but the role follows me: if I need help with something personal or business-related during work hours, that's part of the job.



This is not a task-list VA role. I need someone who thinks, notices, and takes ownership.



Your core responsibilities:

- Manage day-to-day communication with coaching members and agency clients on my behalf — in my voice, to my standard

- Track member engagement and flag disengaged members early, then run reactivation outreach

- Follow up on failed payments and renewals using our existing AI-powered systems

- Complete weekly and monthly reports; keep member data updated

- Collect testimonials, schedule case-study interviews, and ask for referrals

- Surface problems before they become problems, and suggest the SOPs and systems we should build as issues come up

- Personal-assistant support during work hours — scheduling, research, errands that can be done remotely, whatever I need off my plate



Important: most of the mechanical work (payment follow-up, reporting, tracking) is already automated with AI tools. Your job is to USE those tools consistently and apply human judgment where it's needed. You won't be building from scratch — but you must be sharp enough to notice gaps and propose fixes without being told.



HOW ONBOARDING WORKS (FIRST 21 DAYS, PAID)

- Week 1: You shadow me. Watch how I communicate, learn the members, learn the tools.

- Week 2: We build the SOPs and playbook together — you hold the pen.

- Week 3: You take over communications while I watch and give feedback.

- Day 22+: You own it. We meet daily for a 15–30 min 1:1, but I will not manage you task by task.



I think of this seat as the cornerstone of how everything I do runs — hire the right person once, invest in them, and build for years. That word matters; you'll want to remember it when you record your Loom, where I'd like you to work it in naturally within your first minute.



COMPENSATION & TERMS

- $8/hr, full-time (40 hrs/week), paid bi-weekly

- Performance review at 6 months with a $2/hr raise on strong performance

- Hours: 9am–5pm US Pacific Time — confirm you can sustain this schedule long-term before applying

- Time tracking via Hubstaff/Time Doctor

- This must be your ONLY job. No side clients, no other employers.

- 100% long-term, stable role.



REQUIREMENTS

- Fluent, natural written English (you'll be writing to US business owners daily, as me)

- Prior experience supporting a busy professional, executive, or agency owner — with references I can contact

- Extreme attention to detail

- A love of simplifying things — you see a messy process and itch to clean it up

- Proactive: you flag issues, propose solutions, and take accountability when something slips

- Honest, transparent, kind, loyal

- Reliable internet, quiet workspace, own computer



HOW TO APPLY



Submit through the Google Form link below. Applications sent any other way will not be reviewed.



Your application must include:

1. Your resume (PDF)

2. A Loom video (3–5 min): who you are, who you've worked for, and why you're a fit for THIS role specifically

3. Answers to the short questions in the form



Shortlisted candidates complete a paid test assignment (~2.5 hours, paid), then a final Zoom interview.

title: : Scriptwriter for Cinematic History YouTube Channel
description:
Job Title: Scriptwriter for Cinematic History YouTube Channel (Long-term)

Job Type: Part-time, project-based to start (potential full-time)

Salary: $40 per script (negotiable based on experience) — paid per completed 3,000-word script pays up to $80 per script based on quality and can workout a deal to may a flat monthly rate if you seem like a good fit.

Job Description:

I run a growing YouTube channel called History's Last Days. We make cinematic, story-driven history documentaries — each episode follows one person or family through the final day of a famous historical event (Pompeii, the Titanic, the fall of Constantinople). Think movie script, not history lecture.

I'm looking for a scriptwriter who can take an episode topic and deliver a complete, emotionally gripping script.

What you'll do:



Research the historical event using reliable sources and keep every fact accurate

Write one ~3,000-word narration script per episode (about 20 minutes of video) following our episode template: cold-open hook, 4 acts, epilogue

Write in present tense, second person, with strong emotional stakes ("You are standing in the forum when the sky breaks open")

Include a short historical accuracy appendix listing your sources for each major claim

Revise based on feedback (1–2 rounds per script)



Requirements:



Excellent written English — your script gets read aloud word-for-word by a narrator

Genuine interest in history; you know how to check facts, not just paraphrase Wikipedia

Storytelling instinct: pacing, tension, character

Reliable turnaround: 1 script per week

Bonus (not required): experience writing for YouTube documentary/storytelling channels, familiarity with retention-based script structure



How to apply:



Start your application with the word HOURGLASS so I know you read this

Tell me your favorite historical event in 2–3 sentences, written in our style (present tense, one person's point of view)

Link 1–2 writing samples (YouTube scripts preferred, but any narrative writing works)

Your rate per 3,000-word script



Top applicants get a short paid test script.

Decision Discipline (in partnership with TPM / Product)

I'm building a revenue engine on top of an existing Mailchimp account for an indie pop singer-songwriter on the US touring path. She has a real list and a real catalog. What she doesn't have is a lifecycle system that turns subscribers into buyers of tickets, music, and merch. I need someone who has done this before and can show me the numbers.



Starting with a paid trial task so we both confirm fit. Then ongoing.



WHAT YOU'LL OWN



- Mailchimp funnels, customer journeys, and automations end to end: welcome flows, re-engagement, launch sequences, post-purchase

- List growth and list hygiene. Keep the list clean and growing, and build the automations and segmentation an engaged list needs to turn subscribers into ticket, merch, and streaming buyers

- Segmentation that maps to real buying behavior, not renamed lists

- Campaign copy and sequencing built to convert, not just to get opened

- Subscriber-to-buyer conversion: tickets, music, merch, fan membership. The whole spread

- Weekly report: what you shipped, what the numbers did, what you need from us



We stay on Mailchimp. No migration. If you live in Klaviyo or GoHighLevel that's fine, the thinking transfers, but the build happens in Mailchimp.



When you're stuck, you tell me. Disappearing breaks the relationship.



WHAT WE NEED



One thing is non-negotiable: a real revenue track record from
. Not opens. Not "engagement." Money. One account you ran or co-ran where you can show me:



- The dashboard URL

- Subscribers at the start vs at the end

- Revenue attributed to
 over that period

- The timeframe

- What specifically YOU did that moved it: which automations, which segments, which sequences



If you can't show me the numbers, this role isn't for you.



You bring the automation fluency, the segmentation instinct, the copy, and native or near-native English. We onboard you to her voice, her brand, and what we're selling. We don't teach lifecycle marketing.



ENGAGEMENT & PAY



- 10-15 hrs/week, hourly via TimeProof + Payoneer

- Hourly rate depending on your demonstrated revenue track record

- Weekly pay for the first 8 weeks, then bi-weekly

- Bonuses are possible for exceptional work, not guaranteed, not scheduled. If you move revenue past what we asked for, you'll be paid for it. If you don't, you won't. We pay for outcomes.

- Time off: you bill the hours you log. If you'll be unavailable for more than a day, give me a heads-up so I don't think you've disappeared. No paid PTO. This is hourly work.



We provide: Mailchimp access, the voice guide, the brand assets, and a clear picture of what we're selling.

You bring: your automation stack fluency, reliable hardware and internet, and the revenue chops.



WHAT THE ARTIST KEEPS



She owns her songwriting, her personal voice, and final approval on every send that goes out under her name. Brand partnerships, songwriting tie-ins, and identity decisions stay with her. Locked in the contractor agreement, not negotiable.



HOW TO APPLY



1. Include the word STRAWBERRY in your subject line. No STRAWBERRY = I don't read it.

2. The numbers. ONE list you grew and turned into revenue. Dashboard URL, subscribers start vs end, revenue attributed to
, timeframe, and what YOU specifically did. At interview, you'll live-screen-share into that account's reporting and walk me through it. Don't submit an account you can't pull up live. If you need to keep a client's name anonymous, strip the confidential details but keep the numbers. If it's easy, record a Loom screen-share and send me the link.

3. In 2-3 sentences: an
 or lifecycle program you actively admire. What's specifically working? Name the automation, the sequence, the segment. "Great
s" gets rejected.

4. Tell me about a specific campaign or automation YOU ran that flopped. What did you learn?

5. Current bandwidth? How many clients are you working, and in what roles?



ANTI-SCAM



I'll never ask for upfront payment. If you push to move off-platform (WhatsApp,
,
) before we've had a real interview, your application is dropped. Verify this account at onlinejobs.ph/jobseekers/employersearch using 
 personally read every STRAWBERRY application.

title: Virtual Medical Assistant
description:
We are a U.S.-based independent medical examination company seeking a reliable, detail-oriented Virtual Medical Assistant to support our medical examination and reporting process.



This is a remote contractor position ideal for someone with healthcare experience, strong English communication skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to work independently.



Responsibilities



Patient History Collection



* Conduct outbound calls to patients to obtain detailed medical histories

* Ask clear follow-up questions regarding symptoms, injuries, limitations, treatment history, and current complaints

* Document information accurately in narrative form



Medical Report Support



* Transcribe audio recordings into pre-made medical examination templates

* Assist with proofreading and editing medical reports

* Review reports for grammar, spelling, formatting, consistency, and clarity

* Ensure details are accurately transferred into the correct sections of the report



Administrative Support



* Answer and return calls professionally

* Assist with appointment scheduling and calendar management

* Maintain organized records and task updates



Requirements



* Prior healthcare or medical experience required

    (Examples: registered nurse, physician, physical therapist, medical assistant, medical transcriptionist, or similar healthcare background)

* Strong written and spoken English

* Excellent listening and documentation skills

* High attention to detail

* Reliable computer and high-speed internet connection

* Backup internet connection or mobile hotspot preferred

* Quiet, professional workspace

* Ability to work independently and follow instructions

* Professional communication style

* Reliable communication, accurate time tracking, and consistent daily task updates

* Ability to provide timely updates regarding technical or internet issues

* Current or recent NBI clearance preferred



Preferred Qualifications



* RN background preferred

* Experience with medical transcription or medical report editing

* Experience working with U.S.-based healthcare or legal/medical documentation

* Familiarity with medical terminology

* Strong proofreading skills



Compensation



* Compensation based on experience, skill level, reliability, and availability

* Opportunity for long-term growth with the company



Hiring Process



Selected applicants may be asked to complete a short paid test task involving transcription, proofreading, or medical documentation.



How to Apply



Please send the following:



1. Resume/CV

2. Brief summary of your healthcare experience

3. Description of your experience with transcription or medical documentation

4. Your expected hourly rate

5. Your internet speed

6. Your availability and preferred work schedule

7. A short voice recording introducing yourself and describing your healthcare background

8. A short answer to this question: “Why would you be a strong fit for this role?”



We are looking for a dependable long-term tea
mber who can grow with our company.

title: Experienced Full-Stack Developer Needed for Website + Internal Web App Buildout
description:
We are looking for a highly experienced full-stack developer to help us build the technical foundation for a luxury short-term rental and hospitality management company.



We currently have our website and internal dashboard built inside Lovable and connected to Supabase. We need someone who can help us take what we have already built, clean it up, export/manage it through GitHub, host it properly, and continue building it into a real long-term system.



This is not just a basic website role. We need someone who can help with both the public-facing website and the internal web app/dashboard.



Main Responsibilities:



* Review our current Lovable website and internal dashboard

* Help export the app/codebase to GitHub

* Set up proper hosting and deployment outside of Lovable

* Help rebuild or improve the public website so it is fast, clean, and SEO/AEO optimized

* Make sure the website has a strong HTML structure and is built correctly from a technical standpoint

* Connect forms, CRM tools, analytics, Supabase, and other integrations as needed

* Help improve the internal dashboard/admin hub over time

* Build new features, modules, dashboards, automations, and integrations

* Help us eventually add private/direct booking functionality

* Help us build toward an internal AI operating system for the business



Requirements:



* Strong experience with Next.js, React, Node.js, GitHub, and custom web app development

* Experience working with Supabase or similar backend/database tools

* Comfortable with API integrations, hosting, deployment, and database-connected apps

* Able to work with an existing project and improve/clean up what has already been built

* Strong understanding of responsive design, page speed, technical SEO, and clean site structure

* Able to communicate clearly and recommend the best technical path forward

* Must be reliable, detail-oriented, and able to work independently



Bonus Experience:



* Experience with Lovable, Bolt, Replit, or other no-code/prototype tools

* Experience moving projects from no-code/prototype tools into custom code

* Experience building admin dashboards, owner portals, client portals, or internal business tools

* Experience with hospitality, real estate, Airbnb, direct booking sites, or marketplace platforms

* Experience with Stripe, Google Drive/API, CRM integrations, or AI integrations

* Experience with WordPress or Webflow, if that ends up being the right fit for part of the website



About Us:



We are building a luxury hospitality management company focused on high-end short-term rentals, owner experience, guest experience, and operational systems.



The goal is to build a premium public website, a strong internal admin/owner platform, and eventually a private booking experience. We are moving quickly and want someone who can help us build this the right way from the start.



Schedule:



Part-time to start, with the opportunity for ongoing long-term work if it is a good fit.



To Apply:



Please send:



1. A short intro about yourself

2. Examples of websites, dashboards, portals, or web apps you have built

3. Your experience with Next.js, React, Node.js, Supabase, GitHub, and hosting/deployment

4. Any experience you have with Lovable or moving no-code projects into custom code

5. Your hourly rate or project-based pricing

6. Your availability

7. A quick explanation of how you would approach this project



To confirm you read the full post, please include your favorite animal in the subject line.
